AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: This study evaluated both the relation between dobutamine-induced wall motion abnormalities and the physiologic and morphologic features of epicardial coronary artery stenoses and the impact of the extent of the area at risk on the sensitivity of dobutamine echocardiography.

AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: The accuracy of dobutamine echocardiography has traditionally been assessed by comparing results with stenosis geometry. Myocardial fractional flow reserve is a functional index of coronary stenosis severity that takes into account both antero-grade and collateral flow and may therefore be a more appropriate standard for comparison.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Seventy-five patients with normal left ventricular function, good echocardiographic images and an isolated coronary stenosis underwent, within 6 h, dobutamine echocardiography, quantitative coronary angiography and intracoronary pressure measurements. Myocardial fractional flow reserve was calculated as the ratio of mean hyperemic distal coronary to aortic pressure.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The degree of dobutamine-induced dyssynergy correlated significantly with percent diameter stenosis (r = 0.68), area stenosis (r = 0.68) and minimal lumen diameter (r = -0.60) and markedly better with myocardial fractional flow reserve (r = -0.77). However, marked dispersion of the individual data was observed. The sensitivity of dobutamine echocardiography in detecting lesions with a minimal lumen diameter < or = 1 mm and diameter stenosis > or = 50% was 83% and 80%, respectively. All but one patient with a myocardial fractional flow reserve >0.75 had a normal stress test result. Among patients with a myocardial fractional flow reserve < or = 0.75, the sensitivity of dobutamine echocardiography was significantly lower for lesions in vessels with a reference diameter < or = 2.6 mm than for lesions in larger vessels (58% vs. 90%, p = 0.008).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: 1) The magnitude of wall motion abnormalities induced by dobutamine infusion correlates with angiographic and, more closely, with functional indexes of stenosis severity, even though a wide scatter is observed. 2) In patients with a functionally significant stenosis, the amount of myocardium at risk is a critical determinant of the accuracy of dobutamine echocardiography.

Article.ArticleTitle: Dobutamine-induced wall motion abnormalities: correlations with myocardial fractional flow reserve and quantitative coronary angiography.

Journal.Title: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
